title: What the Python SDK sends when it updates a server group

prose.text: The Python SDK builds a server group update body from the group it reads, which drops some fields and omits others.

prose.label: Servers.
prose.text: {{model-has-no-servers-member}} {{servers-sent-only-with-server-ids}} What ZPA does with a PUT that omits servers is open {{gap:servers-omitted-update-effect}}.

The mode defaults across sources are in [[zpa.server-groups.discovery-mode]]. The Terraform update omits the name unless it changed: [[zpa.terraform.resource-fidelity:server-group-update-name-only-on-change]].

checks.do: Whether an update was made through the Python SDK's update_group without server_ids, because the body it builds has no servers member.
Whether the group's servers and dynamicDiscovery are the same after the update as before, by re-reading the group.
Whether the group is attached to many application segments, in which case applications is deliberately left out of the body.

update-reads-then-merges.statement: Python `update_group` first fetches the existing group, starts the request body from its `request_format()`, and then merges the caller's keyword arguments over it.

update-drops-applications.statement: Python `update_group` removes `applications` from the body unless the caller passes it, because, per a code comment, sending it back can exceed the API's payload-size cap for a group tied to many application segments.

quotes: not required to update connector-group / server membership, and round-tripping it can
exceed the API's payload-size cap on tenants where the group is associated with a

model-has-no-servers-member.statement: The Python `ServerGroup` model has no `servers` attribute and its `request_format()` emits no `servers` key, so a body built from it never contains the group's servers.
model-has-no-servers-member.conditions: Absence claim. Searched with `grep -n -i servers zscaler/zpa/models/server_group.py` at the pin: no hits.

servers-sent-only-with-server-ids.statement: In Python `update_group`, `server_ids` is translated to `servers`; a `servers` keyword is merged as given, and without either the body has no `servers` member.

quotes: body["servers"] = [{"id": group_id} for group_id in body.pop("server_ids")]

servers-sent-only-with-server-ids.conditions: Statement changed per verifier: `body.update(kwargs)` also merges a `servers` keyword passed directly.

dynamic-discovery-guard-never-fires.statement: The default that forces `dynamicDiscovery` to true when the key is missing from the body cannot fire on this path, because `request_format()` always sets the key.
dynamic-discovery-guard-never-fires.conditions: Derived from the two files together. It holds while the body starts from `request_format()` and the caller passes no key that deletes `dynamicDiscovery`; keyword arguments can only add or replace keys.

absent-dynamic-discovery-written-as-true.statement: If a GET response omits `dynamicDiscovery`, the model reads it as true and `request_format()` writes true back, so an update can switch a group to dynamic discovery without the caller asking.

quotes: self.dynamic_discovery = config["dynamicDiscovery"] if "dynamicDiscovery" in config else True

absent-dynamic-discovery-written-as-true.conditions: Applies only when the API response lacks the field. Whether it ever does is unknown. The contract's GET response lists dynamicDiscovery ("Defaults to false.") but does not require it (required: configSpace, name), and that documented default is the opposite of the Python model's; the defaults across sources are the divergence zpa.server-groups.discovery-mode:dynamic-discovery-default.

servers-omitted-update-effect.title: Whether a PUT that omits servers clears an explicit server list
servers-omitted-update-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the default injection "can silently clear an explicit server list on a read-modify-write update. Pass `dynamic_discovery=False` explicitly to preserve a static group." The injection is dead code (dynamic-discovery-guard-never-fires), so that advice does not follow. What does follow from the code is that the body never carries servers unless server_ids is passed; whether ZPA then keeps or clears them depends on PUT semantics that no captured source states. Update a static group through update_group without server_ids in a scratch tenant and re-read it.
servers-omitted-update-effect.blocks: saying a Python SDK update loses a static group's servers
